articles.title: Bank of England directors illegally profited from post-abolition enslavement in Cuba
articles.description:
New research finds that the British-led Cobre Mining Company helped industrialise Manchester via copper deposits and enslaved African people

• Slave-trade wealth was embedded in Britain’s financial system, research finds

British businesses run by long-serving directors of the Bank of England profited from “brutal” enslavement in Cuba for decades after slavery’s abolition in the British empire, according to research.

Men and boys were enslaved in prison conditions at the El Cobre copper ore mine near Santiago de Cuba, which supplied British firms during the Industrial Revolution, the historian Chris Evans has found.

Continue reading...

articles.title: South Korea education minister resigns after AI cheating scandal engulfs university exams
articles.description:
Choi Kyo-jin says he ‘failed to prepare adequately’ for entrance exams, which this year had phones banned and checks for cameras hidden in clothing

South Korea’s education minister has resigned after an AI-assisted cheating scandal that erupted in the lead-up to key university entrance exams last week.

The country has been gripped by fears of AI-assisted exam cheating since last Sunday, when the top scorer in a national tax accountant exam confessed to using a miniature camera and smartphone to achieve a near-perfect score, just four days before the crucial university entrance exam, known as the suneung.

Continue reading...

articles.title: Fire at confectionery factory in Indonesia leaves at least three dead and dozens missing
articles.description:
Relatives of the missing victims flocked to the factory’s entrance, seeking updates about their loved ones

A fire at a confectionery factory west of Jakarta has killed three people with 36 remaining missing, an Indonesian rescue official says.

Drone footage showed large parts of the factory destroyed, with the roof collapsed in places and smoke still rising from the complex. Photos and videos shared by rescuers show officers entering the charred building in search of the missing victims on Sunday, with small fires still burning in some spots.

Continue reading...

articles.title: Police say man whose body lay undiscovered in Sydney bushland for 12 days was killed in suspected hit-and-run
articles.description:
Joshua Howard, 31, is believed to have been struck by a car and thrown over the guardrail as he was walking home from a party in Rouse Hill

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The twin brother of a man whose body lay undiscovered for 12 days after he was killed in a suspected hit and run in Sydney says it has left him feeling like half a person.

Joshua Howard was last seen at a bus interchange in Parramatta, in western Sydney, about 10pm on 7 November.

Continue reading...

articles.title: UK-EU food deal hailed by British firms: ‘We’re pretty aligned anyway’
articles.description:
Exporters welcome end in sight for Brexit checks – but are frustrated that implementation will take so long

British producers have broadly welcomed the UK’s deal with the EU, designed to remove the vast majority of physical checks on food, plants and animal products.

The sanitary and phytosanitary (SPS) deal is expected to benefit Britain’s food exporters and will enable UK delicatessens and other small retailers to import European cheese and wine again, something that became economically unviable because of costly Brexit checks.

Continue reading...

articles.title: ‘Serious error of judgment’: outrage over military AI event at Berlin arts complex
articles.description:
Kraftwerk Berlin, part of same development as techno club Tresor, transformed into ‘war room’ for arms firm event

With their cavernous post-industrial venues, teeth-grinding four-by-four beats and bouncers that look like Blade Runner extras, Berlin’s nightclubs trade on a reputation for bleakness. A recent event at one of the city’s most legendary clubland institutions, however, has proven too dystopian even for seasoned techno-heads.

On 11 November, the Kraftwerk Berlin arts complex had its central hall transformed into what visitors described as something resembling a war room, with maps and aerial footage projected on to concrete walls, drones hanging from the ceiling, and guards in flak jackets patrolling the premises with sniffer dogs.

Continue reading...

articles.title: Europe is entering a ‘supercycle’ of national elections. Their outcomes could shake the EU’s foundations
articles.description:
As nationalist, Eurosceptic parties surge in four of the bloc’s biggest member states, the coming year’s polls could test its resilience like never before

In late 1998, Tony Blair was prime minister of Britain, Lionel Jospin was prime minister of France, and Gerhard Schröder had just been elected chancellor of Germany. The EU had 15 member states and pro-European, centre-left parties were in power – either alone or in coalitions – in all but two of them.

Brisk economic growth was lifting living standards. Eastward enlargement was under way. In Washington, Bill Clinton was pursuing the same brand of “third way” centrism as a middle path between free-market capitalism and traditional socialism. The EU felt like it had the tide of history behind it.

Continue reading...

articles.title: Indian opposition party’s youth wing warns of more Meta protests after police clashes
articles.description:
Members of Congress party clashed with police outside tech company’s offices on Friday

The youth wing of India’s main opposition Congress party warned of more protests against Meta’s removal of some of its members’ accounts, a day after clashing with police outside the tech firm’s locals offices.

In Hyderabad on Friday, protesters carrying placards and chanted slogans as they stormed into the building that houses Meta’s offices, smashing plants to the ground and clashing with police, according to footage released by the Indian Youth Congress’s X account.

Continue reading...

articles.title: ‘Just wrong’: British right distances itself from Trump after Putin ‘friend’ post
articles.description:
Reform deputy leader calls Russian leader ‘a murderous dictator’ after US president appears to endorse him

  • UK politics live – latest updates

Reform UK and the Conservatives have distanced themselves from Donald Trump after the US president posted a photo of himself shaking hands with Vladimir Putin with the caption: “My friend.”

The US president had already used the term to describe the Russian president while at last week’s Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen, southern China, where he also met the Chinese president, Xi Jinping.

Continue reading...<

articles.description:
Issue dominates Sunday broadcast round following Friday’s deals on trade and youth mobility

  • Theresa May ‘aghast’ at Andy Burnham’s talk about rejoining EU

European Relations Minister Hamish Falconer on Sky this morning criticised the post from earlier this week, where the US president shared a picture of him embracing Putin under the caption “My Friend”.

Falconer said Putin was a “butcher” and “not a friend of the UK”.

One area where the UK is absolutely and completely united across the whole political spectrum is standing with Ukraine against Russia’s barbaric, illegal war.

So would Vladimir Putin be my friend? No. And he’s not a friend of the UK either.”

The Prime Minister speaks to the president regularly, and is in absolutely no way pulling his punches about the strength of feeling that the U

articles.title: CEO of funding agency for UK science and research criticised by union over cuts
articles.description:
Exclusive: Prospect’s Mike Clancy tells Ian Chapman at UKRI that union has ‘lost confidence’ in his leadership

A trade union that counts scientists and engineers among its members says it has lost confidence in the leader of the UK’s national funding agency for science and research, citing concerns about plans for major cuts.

The letter from Mike Clancy, the general secretary of Prospect, to Ian Chapman, the chief executive of UK Research and Innovation (UKRI), is the latest development in a row over changes in funding for projects and research facilities.

Continue reading...

articles.title: Cloned number plate victims in England and Wales to get new reporting tool
articles.description:
Police launch initiative after steep rise in criminals using method to evade detection and avoid paying penalties

Sandra Yarwood has a file “about 2in thick” of paperwork relating to the 32 driving fines she received this summer after her car’s number plate was cloned.

Yarwood’s black Volkswagen Golf did not move from outside her London home while she was on holiday in Canada, but a similar vehicle with a fraudulent copy of her registration racked up penalty notices totalling £2,560 across five London boroughs.

Continue reading...

articles.title: Closer EU ties will give UK say on Brussels decisions, says Ed Miliband
articles.description:
Foreign secretary says there is clear case to integrate more closely but does not say if he backs talks on possibly rejoining

  • UK politics live – latest updates

Closer links with the EU will mean the UK having a say on decisions made by Brussels, Ed Miliband has argued as ministers faced pressure to move further after Friday’s landmark deal with the EU.

Any timetable for closer integration, including possible talks about the UK rejoining the EU, remains unclear after the Brussels summit, with Andy Burnham saying he would now “brainstorm” over future ties.

Continue reading...

articles.title: They went out to celebrate at a Memphis bar. Then, ICE descended
articles.description:
More than 120 people in the Tennessee city were detained in one of the largest single-day ICE raids in the US in 2026

The date 1 September, or 9/01 Day, is a festive day for Memphians. The date mirrors the city’s 901 area code, and gives residents a reason to come together to celebrate the city and the people who love it. When 9/01 Day falls on a weekday, as it did this year, the celebration starts the weekend prior, extending the festivities. Groups across the city hosted celebrations featuring food vendors, DJs, musicians and members of the Memphis Grizzlies, the local NBA team, while dozens of local businesses offered $9.01-themed specials.

But for the families of 121 people, this past 1 September will be remembered for a different reason – just days prior, US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officers detained their friends and relatives, cond

articles.title: Conservative media weighs its future as cracks emerge in Trump’s movement
articles.description:
Two weeks after Democrats flipped Congress, conservative outlets are having conversations on whether to distance themselves from Trump or double down on Maga

As a so-called “blue wave” crashed across the country on the night of 3 November, conservative hosts and commentators on Fox News displayed an almost virtuosic ability to avoid directly blaming Donald Trump for the Republican party’s defeat, instead pinning the blame on impertinent voters who didn’t grasp the strength of the economy.

“In some sense, Mr Trump was too successful in the first year and didn’t sell it enough in the second year,” said Larry Kudlow, a Fox Business Network host who served as the president’s director of the National Economic Council during his first administration.

Continue readin

articles.title: Arizona grandfather hailed as a hero after finding missing toddler in desert
articles.description:
Jay Stewart joined search party after two-year-old Vella Campillo wandered off into desert from front yard of home

An Arizona granddad has been formally recognized as a hero after recently volunteering to help search for a toddler who wandered off alone into the desert while wearing only a diaper – and finding her safely within several hours curled up under a bush, leading to her rescue.

“I’ll never forget it as long as I live,” Jay Stewart said of recovering Vella Campillo, two, while recalling the moment at a news conference held later. “I’ve never wanted to find something so bad in my life – or somebody to find her, anybody to find her.”

articles.title: Man found dead on Flinders Island believed to have been shot by officer, police say
articles.description:
The sergeant, who was shot, fired his weapon a number of times after alleged ‘targeted’ attack outside island’s police station

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A police officer who was shot outside a remote Tasmanian police station is alleged to have shot and killed his attacker in response to what authorities believe was a “targeted” incident.

Tasmania police deputy commissioner, Jonathan Higgins, said the sergeant had just come off shift at Whitemark police station on Flinders Island, which is north-east of the Tasmanian mainland. He had parked and gotten out of his police vehicle when he was shot at about 9.45pm on Saturday, Higgins told reporters on Sunday.

articles.title: Victorian Greens win injunction over how-to-vote cards mimicking party’s branding but preferencing it last
articles.description:

  • Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast

The Victorian Greens have won a supreme court injunction to stop an independent candidate from handing out how to vote cards that mimic their branding and urge people to preference it last.

The decision has been welcomed by the party’s leader, Ellen Sandell, who said the flyers distributed by people wearing the exact same colour shirts as genuine Greens volunteers had already misled voters.

articles.title: ‘No time for a culture war’: Victoria’s electricity supply is at risk. Can it avoid power shortages and bill shocks?
articles.description:
State faces electricity supply gap when Yallourn coal-fired power station closes in 2028 as experts warn neither Labor nor the Coalition has adequate plans

  • Sign up for climate and environment editor Adam Morton’s free Clear Air newsletter here

Victoria’s electricity supply will be at risk when a major power plant shuts in 2028 and neither major party is offering a plan at this month’s state election to deal with it, experts have warned.

All parties concede the giant Yallourn coal plant, which has operated in the Latrobe Valley since the 1970s and supplies a fifth of Victoria’s energy, is at the end of its functional life and will shut in less than two years. Analysts say the parties vying to run the state are failing to properly explain how they will fill the power shortfall the closure will cre

articles.title: Fred Nile, former NSW politician and figurehead of the rightwing Christian Democratic party, dies aged 92
articles.description:
Controversial figure frequently took positions against drug use, abortion and homosexuality, but in later years supported legislation expunging homosexual convictions

  • Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast

The former New South Wales MP and longstanding figurehead of the rightwing Christian Democratic party, the Rev Fred Nile, has died aged 92.

Nile was a member of the NSW legislative council for more than 40 years. He first entered the state’s upper house in 1981 and retired after unsuccessfully contesting the 2023 election.

articles.description:
Body of a man in his 20s discovered by police who were sent to investigate the shooting of an officer, who is in a serious but stable condition

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

An on-duty police officer has been shot and a man found dead nearby as police investigate two firearm incidents in a tiny Tasmanian town.

The officer was working at Whitemark police station on Flinders Island, north-east of the island of Tasmania, when he was shot at about 9.45pm on Saturday night.

articles.description:
A government in office for more than two years is finally forced to take responsibility and seemingly no longer able to blame its Labor predecessors

At the beginning of another Queensland parliamentary sitting week, anonymous sources were out in force, this time background briefing against the state’s Labor leader, Steven Miles.

It is no great revelation to observers of Queensland politics that Miles, still seemingly bruised from his election loss two years ago, has struggled to find his feet as opposition leader. articles.title: Cigarettes on silver platters at Bondi ‘clean’ beauty business lip gloss launch referred for investigation
articles.description:
Copini Beauty referred to New South Wales health regulators, while federal government says it is ‘deeply concerned’

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

An Australian beauty company that promotes “clean” ingredients “free from skin irritants” has been referred to state health regulators after appearing to offer cigarettes to guests at a beachside lip gloss launch.

Photos from an event held earlier in November at a venue in Bondi, Sydney show what appears to be loose cigarettes without health warnings on a tiered silver platter alongside a bowl of lip glosses.

Continue reading...

articles.title: Australian neo-Nazis among far-right groups raising hundreds of thousands via global crowdfunding platform
articles.description:
GiveSendGo has been accused of facilitating the financing of extremism, but the platform says it does not ‘condone racism, discrimination, hate speech, or violence of any kind’

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Australian neo-Nazis have raised hundreds of thousands of dollars on the global crowdfunding platform GiveSendGo, which has been accused of facilitating the financing of hate and extremism.

Of the 68 Australian fundraisers on the site, the White Australia party has raised the fourth-highest amount of money with $200,000 for its high court battle to overturn its

articles.title: Man charged with attempted murder after councillor stabbed in Bradford
articles.description:
Arfan Ali, 31, has also been charged with assault and possession of an offensive weapon in a public place

A man has been charged with attempted murder after a local councillor was stabbed while working in the community in Bradford, police have said.

Arfan Ali, 32, is accused of attacking Ibrar Ali, 52, at about 11am on Thursday in the West Yorkshire city.

Continue reading...

articles.title: Suffolk village votes to ‘leave the UK’ over plans to house asylum seekers nearby
articles.description:
Local MP says legitimate criticisms of asylum housing plans are being co-opted by opposition parties ‘stirring up racial discord’

Residents of a Suffolk village have voted to “leave the UK” in a referendum held in response to government plans to house 930 asylum seekers at a nearby former military base.

Approximately 500 people in Barnham were eligible to take part in the symbolic vote on Saturday. There were 257 votes for independence, 16 against and one spoiled ballot.

Continue reading...

articles.title: Two groups verify mathematician’s claim that Claude helped prove mathematics problem
articles.description:
Anthropic’s Levent Alpöge says it took six weeks for him using the AI tool to solve 19th-century Riemann hypothesis

A mathematician at Anthropic has said that the San Francisco-based artificial intelligence (AI) company’s software has helped crack one of the most important unsolved problems in mathematics – and experts say the claim checks out.

Levent Alpöge, a Turkish American mathematician, on Friday posted a note on his personal website saying that Claude, the AI software, had helped prove the Riemann hypothesis. He says that Claude helped develop a solution to the problem during the course of about six weeks.

Continue reading...

articles.title: Louisiana man charged with killing woman on hiking trail and murdering co-worker with crossbow
articles.description:
Jared Schurr arrested in Mississippi after Lizeht Rodriguez and Woodrow Scott died in otherwise unrelated killings

A man recently strangled a woman to death whom he did not know along a hiking trail north of New Orleans – then killed his co-worker with a crossbow two days later before being arrested in Mississippi after a police chase, authorities allege.

Jared Schurr, 36, faces counts of second-degree murder in the killings of Lizeht Rodriguez, 24, and Woodrow Scott, 37, on 11 and 13 November, respectively, investigators said on Saturday.

Continue reading...

articles.title: Alleged Mexican drug cartel boss ‘El Chapo Isidro’ arrested in special forces raid
articles.description:
Fausto Isidro Meza Flores was one of FBI’s most wanted fugitives and evaded capture for more than a decade

The Mexican military captured one of the FBI’s top 10 most wanted fugitives during a special forces raid in the Mexican state of Sinaloa on Friday night.

Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, known as “El Chapo Isidro”, was arrested along with two other alleged leaders of his gang after a gun battle that sparked widespread panic in the city of Guasave.

articles.title: International UN talks on controlling use of autonomous weapons collapse
articles.description:
Week-long efforts fail to establish negotiating mandate on AI warfare after Russian ‘filibustering’

Week-long efforts to agree a negotiating mandate for a legally binding international treaty to control the use of autonomous weapons collapsed just before 5am after all-night talks failed to overcome Russian objections.

Despite an overwhelming majority of states at the UN’s Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons (CCW) in Geneva wanting to agree a negotiating mandate leading to a legally binding treaty, the need for consensus forced the conference to adopt a much weaker option.

Continue reading...

articles.title: British man recalls ‘despair’ over son’s death after fall from Cyprus window
articles.description:
Joshua Foster tells of moment he ‘lost control’ of two-year-old when he fell from fourth storey of hotel

A British father who was fined by the courts after his two-year-old son fell from a fourth-floor window during a family holiday in Cyprus has recalled his “despair” when the boy slipped from his grasp.

Joshua Foster was handed a €3,000 (£2,500) penalty after he pleaded guilty to a charge of causing death through a reckless, rash or dangerous act. Prosecutors in Cyprus had refused to drop the case against him.

Continue reading...

articles.title: Denmark to expel Russian diplomat over alleged plot to kill US-Ukrainian rapper
articles.description:
Moscow intelligence thought to be behind plan to kill musician Kyivstoner before concert in Denmark

Denmark’s foreign minister has said Russia’s defence attache in Copenhagen would be expelled after Moscow was suspected of being behind an attempted killing of a US-Ukrainian rapper.

“We have just summoned the Russian ambassador to the ministry of foreign affairs and notified him of the government’s decision to expel the Russian defence attache from Denmark,” Lars Løkke Rasmussen told a news conference. The expulsion will happen within seven days.

Continue reading...

articles.title: Cold gives way to rain in parts of UK as weather warning issued for south-west England
articles.description:
Flood alerts in place and risk of power cuts as more than 100mm predicted to fall on Dartmoor on Sunday

Cold snaps are to make way for heavy rain in some parts of the country as the Met Office issued a weather warning for south-west England.

It said there will be a slow-moving band of rain moving across Devon and Cornwall, with more than 100mm due to fall on Dartmoor. The warning will be in place from 6am on Sunday until midnight.

Continue reading...

articles.title: Princess of Wales speaks about impact of cancer diagnosis in BBC film Heal
articles.description:
Documentary records Catherine taking on Three Peaks challenge and finding ‘sense of hope alongside uncertainty’

The Princess of Wales has spoken candidly about the impact of her cancer diagnosis in a BBC documentary to be aired later this month.

“Cancer does change you,” Catherine, 44, says in the trailer for the 30-minute programme. “It changes your body. It changes you physically, but there’s a much, much deeper part to what a cancer diagnosis shifts in you.”

Continue reading...

articles.title: Reform UK considers pact with Restore Britain to overcome stalling performance in polls
articles.description:
Thursday’s byelection in Castle Bromwich will be latest test for Nigel Farage’s party as rival eats into support

Voters go to the polls in the village of Castle Bromwich in the West Midlands on Thursday in a little-noticed election that is the latest test for Reform at a time when it is particularly vulnerable.

Yet, while it is the Conservatives who are edging ahead in recent polls, the decisive difference could well be the performance of Restore Britain – the hard-right party set up by Rupert Lowe after the MP fell out with Nigel Farage.

Continue reading...

articles.title: ‘Music was our teacher’: the sound system pioneers reviving the scene in Manchester and beyond
articles.description:
Manchester-based Megatone Sound Foundation and Baron Turbo Charge have rejuvenated the culture to offer a sense of belonging and empowerment

For a generation of young Black Mancunians, some of the history lessons that mattered most were not taught in classrooms, but through towering stacks of amps and speakers, turntables and Jamaican records.

“We didn’t know where we fit in. We didn’t know our history. Our parents were busy working two or three jobs,” says Errol “Barzy” Beaumont, a founder member of Baron Turbo Charge, Manchester’s long-running reggae sound system. “It was the records – Burning Spear, Bob Marley, Culture, that were telling us about our culture, which wasn’t on the school curriculum. For us, the sound system was not just entertainment – it was an education.”

articles.title: Trump orders contractors to check with White House over any congressional inquiries
articles.description:
Anticipating flood of Democratic requests, US president issues executive order in attempt to stymie oversight efforts

Donald Trump is directing federal contractors and subcontractors to consult with his administration about inquiries they receive from Congress and to withhold any communications that the White House considers privileged, according to an executive order issued late Friday.

The companies must also coordinate with the White House and US agencies on “appropriate responses” to any such requests, the order says. If they fail to comply, the White House warns, their contracts could be terminated and their future work with the federal government suspended.

Continue reading...

articles.title: Vance stops short of endorsing Trump’s claim that Iran was close to nuclear weapon
articles.description:
US vice-president says it’s not his place to second-guess the president, but refrains from endorsing Trump’s claim

At a White House news conference on Friday, JD Vance stopped short of endorsing Donald Trump’s claim that Iran was so close to obtaining a nuclear weapon in February that it was essential for the US to go to war with the Islamic republic.

In the White House briefing room, Trump was asked about reporting this week that he was unhappy with the US vice-president’s statement blaming Republican losses in the midterm elections on the Iran war.

articles.description:
Death adds to national measles outbreak that recently cost the US its measles elimination status after 26 years

Virginia reported its first measles-associated death of 2026 on Friday, involving a child who tested positive for the infectious disease, the state’s health department said.

The department said the child was age four or younger. It did not disclose additional details, including the child’s vaccination status, citing the family’s privacy.

articles.title: SNL’s skit Sister captures the quiet agony of caregiving for women: ‘I’ve never felt seen like that’
articles.description:
The viral satirization of the caregiving burden left to women and daughters hit home for many viewers

The Saturday Night Live sketch, titled Sister quickly went viral this week for its satirization of the burden that women and daughters face to take care of aging family members. In the parody commercial, comedian John Mulaney touts the benefit of “Sister”, who he describes as “a live-in 24/7 elder care provider that is completely free, and also your sister” .

“Now I don’t have to worry about dad getting the care and attention he needs because my sister will do it, and I can get back to my life, and the stuff I like to do,” Mulaney says, as the sister, played by cast member Jane Wickline, gives their father’s medication to him.

articles.title: Haitians excited but uneasy as El Salvador troops fight gangs
articles.description:
Foreign combatants in Port-au-Prince welcomed by many after years of gang control but some fear offensive could exacerbate volatile situation

A bullet-peppered mural of the Haitian striker Emmanuel Sanon covers the facade of Port-au-Prince’s main football ground. But more than two years have passed since any sports stars graced the pitch.

In 2024, as the surrounding city was almost entirely captured by heavily armed gangs, Sylvio Cator stadium – where football greats including Brazil’s Ronaldo and Roberto Carlos once played – also fell under criminal control, its dilapidated red and blue stands used as an outpost by fighters working for a gang boss called Izo. articles.title: China commits to low-carbon electrification and help for others to improve
articles.description:
Exclusive: Countries at Cop31 are being urged to commit to deriving 35% of their energy from electricity by 2035

  • Cop31 live – latest updates

China is pushing for rapid electrification of its economy using low-carbon energy and will help other countries do the same, a senior member of the Chinese delegation at the Cop31 UN climate summit has said.

Wang Yi, a professor of energy and environment policy at the Chinese Academy of Sciences and a senior adviser to China’s government, said: “End-use electrification is a very clear direction. We can follow this direction while making the source of electricity clean. That’s the way to go forward.”

articles.title: Teenager allegedly organised arsons and kidnapping on Signal during Melbourne hospitality wars
articles.description:
Victoria police say boy, 17, communicated with offenders under username ‘Onepercent’

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Victorian police allege a 17-year-old boy tasked others to carry out a series of arsons, home invasions and a mistaken identity kidnapping that resulted in the partial amputation of a victim’s finger during Melbourne’s hospitality wars.

The boy, who was arrested on Friday afternoon, allegedly communicated with the offenders under the username “Onepercent” on the encrypted communications app Signal.

Continue reading...

articles.title: As the Coalition stares down One Nation in NSW, a new threat is rising: independents
articles.description:
The opposition’s struggle is creating an opportunity for progressive independents who are boosted by shrewd political operator Chris Minns

  • Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast

The New South Wales Coalition is facing a renewed threat to its heartland seats on Sydney’s north shore.

This time, the threat is from independent candidates – and they’re backed by the same community activists who put a swathe of teal independents into federal parliament.

articles.title: Rejoining EU ‘on the table’ as UK makes deals on trade and young people
articles.description:
All options open in future talks, says Ed Miliband, while prime minister hails ‘a good day for Britain and Europe’

The UK rejoining the EU could be on the table in informal discussions between Andy Burnham and European leaders in Brussels, Ed Miliband has said.

The foreign secretary said “all options” would be examined in the process, after the prime minister agreed deals on trade and young people with the bloc on Friday.

Continue reading...

articles.title: ‘So what if there’s a hole? It hasn’t collapsed’: Kyiv residents unbothered by Russian attacks on city’s bridges
articles.description:
Despite dodging tears in the tarmac, people are confident in city’s infrastructure – and will not worry about what has not happened yet

Mykola expects to drive his battered beige passenger minibus 20 to 24 times a day past the holes in the road on Kyiv’s damaged Northern Bridge that were caused by a Russian ballistic missile attack on Tuesday.

Buses are now the only motor transport allowed across the normally busy multi-lane crossing, though on their way into the city centre they have to skirt the tears in the tarmac, using the only functioning lane to get by.

Continue reading...

articles.title: Tourists are throwing fewer coins into Rome’s Trevi fountain – is €2 entry fee to blame?
articles.description:
Charity that collects the coins says donations are down by £200,000 after a barrier was put in place to restrict access

When Jeff Clinton, an American visiting Rome with his wife for the first time, found a US one-cent coin on a street close to Termini train station, he knew precisely what he was going to do with it. “I’ll throw it into the Trevi fountain,” said Clinton, holding the copper coin in the palm of his hand as the couple admired the landmark.

He was well aware of the tradition among tourists of tossing a coin over their shoulder and into the waters of the baroque masterpiece, in a ritual fabled to ensure a return visit to the city or make other dreams come true.

Continue reading...

articles.title: When you see smoke, run: Rohingya who escaped Myanmar’s genocide tell their stories
articles.description:
Survivors recount rivers red with blood and burning nearby villages serving as an urgent warning to flee their homes

Smoke was often the signal to run – seen from a distance, it was the indication for Rohingya that a neighbouring village was under attack and that theirs would be next.

In other places, they saw the rivers run red and would pull out the bodies, perform quick burial rites and then flee.

Continue reading...

articles.title: Black Friday deals for liquid Brazilian butt lifts criticised over safety fears
articles.description:
Experts say BBLs and other cosmetic procedures can be risky and seasonal offers at clinics in England could make people rush decisions

Clinics in England are promoting seasonal deals – including for Black Friday – on liquid Brazilian butt lifts (BBLs), despite concerns about the risks of the procedure.

The government is consulting on limiting liquid BBLs, vampire facials and deep chemical peels in England to qualified healthcare professionals. The proposals follow the death of Alice Webb, a 33-year-old mother of five, after a botched liquid BBL in a Gloucester salon in 2024. Her family have called for laws against “cosmetic cowboys” to be introduced before more people die.

articles.title: Telegraph departures signal concerns over direction under Axel Springer’s ownership
articles.description:
Insiders say they only see cuts, with no discernible long-term strategy, since title’s purchase by German media firm

A spate of prominent departures and years of public battling over its ownership have ensured the Telegraph’s newsroom has been no stranger to internal intrigue and speculation in recent times.

Even by its own high standards, however, its offices have been fraught with rumours about its leadership this week.

Continue reading...

articles.title: Letby trial doctor barred from treating patients was expert witness in another case
articles.description:
Prof Peter Hindmarsh played key role in conviction of two Birmingham parents whose son died after diabetes episode

A doctor who gave expert evidence that helped to convict Lucy Letby, and who was barred during the trial from treating patients, was then instructed as an expert witness in another prosecution.

The Guardian revealed this week that Prof Peter Hindmarsh was excluded from clinical practice in March 2023, during the main trial of Letby, by his employer, University College London hospitals trust (UCLH). The jury, who five months later convicted Letby of the murder of seven babies, were never told.

Continue reading...

articles.title: Campaigners back call for scrutiny of consent laws by Joanne Young
articles.description:
Experts say no law states third-party consent is a valid defence and call for public debate and further education

Campaigners have welcomed a call for scrutiny of consent laws by a survivor of drug-facilitated rape but said action must also focus on wider issues around sexual assault.

Joanne Young, who was drugged and raped by her husband and sexually abused by men he invited into their home, warned of “serious questions about how the law deals with consent”.

Continue reading...

articles.title: New Orleans Catholic clergy abuse survivors begin receiving payments from $305m bankruptcy settlement
articles.description:
Arrival of payments in contentious legal saga that began in 2020 is ‘a weight off my shoulders’, one survivor said

Hundreds of clergy sexual abuse survivors have received more than half of the $305m bankruptcy settlement that the archdiocese of New Orleans reached with them last year, a milestone that marks the beginning of the end of a years-long legal saga.

The trustee overseeing the settlement fund, Don Massey, confirmed on Friday that $180m had been distributed to 450 of about 740 survivors, either directly or through their lawyers if they retained legal representation. Massey said he and his staff are working hard to get payments in the rest of the survivors’ hands by the end of the year but are still waiting on hundreds of distribution forms from survivors and their lawyers.

articles.title: Did Democrats fail Florida? Angie Nixon on ‘missed opportunity’ in midterms
articles.description:
The party invested in key battlegrounds, netting stunning wins at the expense of candidates in Florida and Louisiana

To call it a blue wave, said the Florida governor, Ron DeSantis, would be an epic understatement. The midterm elections were “the political equivalent of a meteor strike”. But one state, DeSantis added with pride, was able to “hold the line”. And that state was Florida.

On a night when almost everything else went right for Democrats, David Jolly fell short by 1.3 percentage points against Republican Byron Donalds, who will become Florida’s first Black governor, while Angie Nixon, bidding to become the state’s first Black senator,

articles.title: ‘A new record for entertainment’: Grand Theft Auto VI sales hit $3.8bn on first day of release, developer says
articles.description:
The announcement from Rockstar Games would mean GTA VI has already earned more than the entire box office run of the highest-grossing film of all time

Grand Theft Auto VI generated $3.79bn in retail sales on its first day, publisher Rockstar Games has announced, calling it the biggest launch for any entertainment product in history.

The worldwide figure was based on company estimates through the end of the day Thursday, the day the game launched. Rockstar said also it had sold 32.5m units of the game on prerelease, setting a record across platforms.

Continue reading...

articles.title: Trump threatens ‘tremendous penalties’ for US tech firms that build datacenters abroad
articles.description:
President gives wide-ranging White House press conference and says he has ‘fantastic relationships’ with Putin and Xi

Donald Trump threatened on Friday to impose “tremendous penalties” on American tech companies that build datacenters outside the US, though he gave no details and told reporters he had not yet informed his own officials about the plan.

In a discursive press conference from the White House briefing room, Trump also said he would “look into” the report that Iran had been planning to possibly detonate a “dirty bomb” in Washington DC, and backed JD Vance over comments the vice-president made blaming Republican midterm losses on the Iran war.

Continue reading...

articles.title: Victorian Greens seek urgent injunction over how-to-vote cards mimicking party’s branding but preferencing it last
articles.description:
Exclusive: Independent candidate Tosh-Jake Finnigan’s cards instruct people to vote in a way that would benefit Liberal party

  • Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast

The Victorian Greens are seeking an urgent injunction from the supreme court to stop an independent candidate distributing how-to-vote cards that allegedly mimic the party’s branding and urge people to preference it last.

As prepoll opened on Wednesday morning, Tosh-Jake Finnigan’s campaign team handed out how-to-vote cards that used the minor party’s colour scheme, font and triangle logo with the banner “Vote 1 Green Values”.

articles.title: NSW passes Mount Pleasant coalmine law as Greens claim change an attempt to head off One Nation
articles.description:
Labor says allowing mine to increase production reflects ‘gravity of situation facing hundreds of workers’ – but critics call it ‘unprecedented and dangerous’

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The New South Wales government has passed special legislation to allow a coalmine in the Hunter Valley to increase production by 32% in its final act of parliament before the March state election, in which the region will be a key battleground for One Nation.

After a marathon session in the legislative council on Friday, the Minns government and the Coalition voted at 1.36am on Saturday morning to allow the Mount Pleasant mine to increase its annual extraction rate from 12.5MT to 16.5MT until 2032.

articles.title: Man accused of sparking deadly Los Angeles wildfire found guilty
articles.description:
Verdict in case against former Uber driver Jonathan Rinderknecht comes after first trial ended with hung jury

The 30-year-old accused of sparking the deadly Palisades fire in Los Angeles was found guilty of two federal arson charges in a Friday verdict that came months after his first trial concluded with a hung jury.

For two weeks, a fresh batch of jurors listened to prosecutors mount their case against Jonathan Rinderknecht.

Continue reading...

articles.title: Trump turns White House press conference into a 2028 succession audition
articles.description:
The president appeared to put Vance and Rubio through their paces as potential successors, though Stephen Miller unexpectedly stole the spotlight

“Which of you shall we say doth love us most?”

The ageing King Lear’s question to his daughters, expecting them to compete for his favour and carve up his kingdom, hovered in the White House press briefing room on Friday.

articles.title: ‘A source of inspiration’: California celebrates the late civil rights icon Dolores Huerta
articles.description:
A public vigil and celebration of life honor the civil rights activist and co-founder of United Farm Workers union

Hundreds of people came out to honor and celebrate the life and legacy of the California civil rights activist Dolores Huerta at a celebration-of-life event Friday in Bakersfield.

Huerta’s daughter Lori de Leon thanked attendees for their support during her mother’s passing, highlighting the widespread tributes and communities gathering in her honor.

Continue reading...

articles.title: Republican senator blocks Trump cyber nominee over January 6 denial
articles.description:
Thom Tillis move comes after Michael LoSapio, nominated for Cisa role, told hearing ‘I don’t believe it was an attack’

Senator Thom Tillis, the outgoing North Carolina Republican who is due to be replaced by a Democrat, has reportedly blocked a confirmation vote on Donald Trump’s nominee to lead a key US cybersecurity agency, Michael LoSapio, after he denied during a hearing that the Capitol was attacked on January 6 2021.

Tillis, who declined to run for re-election and after repeated clashes with Trump’s, confirmed to HuffPost on Friday that he has placed a hold on LoSapio’s nomination to serve as a director of the US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Agency (Cisa). His block on the nomination will prevent it from being included in a package of nominees to be voted on next month, before the Republicans lose their majority in the Sen

articles.title: Judge approves $7.25bn Bayer payout to settle claims that Roundup causes cancer
articles.description:
German company faced 65,000 claims from people who said they developed cancer after using weedkiller

A Missouri judge on Friday approved Bayer’s $7.25bn settlement of lawsuits alleging that its weedkiller Roundup causes cancer, potentially resolving litigation that has weighed on the German company for close to a decade.

Judge Timothy Boyer of a state court in St Louis found the settlement “fair, reasonable and adequate”.

Continue reading...

articles.title: In a year of AI solving maths problems, Anthropic may have just solved the biggest
articles.description: A mathematician at Anthropic says he used an AI to prove the famed Riemann hypothesis, though verification will take some time.

articles.title: Mamdani announces plan to close New York's Rikers Island jail by 2032
articles.description: Plans to shutter the troubled facility date back to 2019, when the city council first voted to close it but delays arose over where to place inmates.

articles.description: The Pentagon has released an eighth tranche of UFO records, which includes three video clips recorded in 2020, 2023 and 2026.

articles.description: How convicted fraudsters made millions from detained immigrants, evaded efforts to shut down their bail business and left migrants behind bars.

articles.title: ANC fights to keep control of South Africa's key cities after election setback
articles.description: The ANC appears reluctant to replicate its national power-sharing deal with the pro-business DA at the local level.
